title: The bucket
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. A bucket of blackberries on the frame shop's counter when Wood gets there. From Gully, left on the step. The owner eats one. Says they're from the mill. Wood asks how she knows. She says everyone knows the mill's berries. The town has a taste.

panels.composition: The frame shop. A bucket of blackberries on the counter. The OWNER with one, eating it. WOOD in the door.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses eating a blackberry from a bucket on a shop counter as a young man enters, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The bucket. Purple on the fingers. Stains on the counter.

image.prompt: close on a bucket of blackberries with purple stains on a wooden counter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood eating one. Tasting it. The mill. He can taste it too. He didn't know.

image.prompt: a young man eating a blackberry with a look of recognition, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The bucket by the mat cutter. Wood cutting with purple fingers. A mat with a thumbprint. The owner keeps that one. She says it's a signature.

image.prompt: a young man cutting a mat with berry-stained fingers, a purple thumbprint on the cream board, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Everyone knows the mill's berries.' The purple thumbprint mat, kept.
